title: Capability Envelope and Scope-Boundary Matrix for Tenant-Aware RBAC v2
creator: Priya Shah
description: Objective: Define a pragmatic, auditable RBAC v2 role model that supports tenant-delimited resources, cross-tenant admin controls, and SSO/SAML attribute mapping. Output will be a spec (this ticket) + implementation tasks for the role resolver, policy evaluator, migration helpers, and audit enrichment hooks. Core idea: represent permissions as a combination of a capability envelope (what actions are allowed), a scope-boundary (where those actions apply), and an attribution token (why/when an elevation was granted). The design must enable deny-by-default, easy read of effective permissions for debugging, efficient evaluation in the runtime serving path, and compact audit events that capture scope provenance.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page matrix mapping canonical capabilities (read/write/list/admin) to resource lanes (org, tenant, project, model, deployment) with explicit deny rules
Policy evaluator pseudocode showing evaluation order, short-circuiting, and cache key design for fast path in the serving runtime
SAML/SSO attribute mapping guide and examples for provisioning role bindings and transient elevations
Audit schema: example event payloads for allow/deny decisions, elevation events, and delegated admin actions with scope provenance fields
Migration checklist to move legacy role assignments into capability envelopes without causing immediate permission surge
implementation_notes: Introduce 'capability envelope' as a stable enum of actions (e.g., model.infer, model.deploy, deployment.bump, billing.view) rather than verb strings to avoid drift
Scope boundaries are represented as typed predicates (tenantId, projectId, resourceTag) and composed into an ordered lattice for evaluation
Evaluator returns both decision and 'explain' vector for UI/console tracing; the explain vector must be compact and safe for logs
Use short-lived elevation tokens for breakglass with audit hooks that require justification text and originating SSO session id
Plan for server-side cache invalidation on role binding changes; include a push-notify channel from control-plane to serving runtime
migration_plan: Phase 1: inventory existing role bindings and map to capability envelopes using automated heuristics (scripted mapping + manual review for ambiguous bindings). Phase 2: deploy evaluator in shadow mode to produce effective-permissions reports for customers and internal dashboards. Phase 3: opt-in pilot for internal teams with canary rollout. Phase 4: flip enforce gate and retire legacy resolver. Provide rollback by reapplying legacy bindings and forcing cache purge.
test_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluator covering composition, deny precedence, and scope intersection/union
Integration tests simulating SSO provisioning events and transient elevation flows with audit assertions
Load tests for common fast-path permission checks to ensure <3ms median added latency per request at 99th percentile under target QPS
Fuzz tests for conflicting role bindings and garbage collection of stale elevations
rollout_steps: 1) Merge spec and publish in internal design repo with diagram links
2) Implement evaluator library and run in shadow mode for 2 weeks while recording explain vectors
3) Provide console view for effective permissions and admin explain traces for select internal teams
4) Run migration scripts for non-privileged bindings and invite teams to opt into new model
5) Enable enforcement for a small set of infra APIs, monitor audit logs and error budgets, then expand scope
6) Complete SSO attribute mapping docs and enable automated provisioning connectors in Enterprise onboarding flow
open_questions: Should capability envelopes be extensible by plugins or locked to a canonical set maintained by Platform Security?
How to represent templated resource sets (e.g., 'all models tagged analytics/*') in the scope lattice without leading to slow queries?
What level of detail is acceptable in audit events to satisfy compliance while not leaking sensitive IDs in logs shipped to third-party analytics?
Do we require tenant-scoped admin roles to implicitly include 'view' on billing-related resources, or treat billing as orthogonal?
